Treatment of stiff person syndrome with chronic plasmapheresis
B. De la Casa-Fages, F. Anaya, F. Grandas (Madrid, Spain)
Objective: To report on two cases of stiff person syndrome (SPS)
with clinical response to chronic plasmapheresis.
Background: SPS is an autoimmune movement disorder charac-
terized by muscle stiffness, rigidity and stimuli induced spasms
affecting axial and proximal limb muscles. Anti-GAD antibodies are
found in 60-80% of patients. EMG shows continuous motor unit ac-
tivity (CMUA) in affected muscles. Immunomodulatory treatments
have been tried with variable results.
Methods: Patient 1 A 61-year-old woman with vitiligo and perni-
cious anemia, presented with a ten-year history of progressive rigidity of
trunk and limbs and spasms affecting abdominal and paraspinal muscles.
Physical exam revealed hyperlordosis, stiffness,spasms of axial muscles
and slow gait. A brain and spine MRI were normal. Blood test revealed
anti-GAD-65 antibodies >2000 U/ml (normal < 10). EMG showed
CMUA in paraspinal muscles. Screening for neoplasia was negative.
Treatment with baclofen, valproic acid, diazepam, botulinum toxin, IV
immunoglobulins and IV metilprednisolone produced mild improve-
ment. Weekly plasmapheresis sessions were started. Patient 2 A5 0 -
year-old man with diabetes and vitiligo had a 22-year history of progres-
sive rigidity of trunk and hips, gait difﬁculty and falls. He also had sen-
sorial stimuli-induced spasms. Physical exam showed hypertonia of par-
aspinal and abdominal muscles with lumbar hyperlordosis. A brain and
spine MRI were normal. Anti-GAD-65 antibodies titers were >2000 U/
ml. EMG showed CMUA in paraspinal muscles and lower limbs. He
was treated with clonazepam, diazepam, IV metilprednisolone and aza-
tioprine with mild improvement. IV immunoglobulins were not effec-
tive. Weekly plasmapheresis was started.
Results: Patient 1 Clinical improvement was observed after ﬁve
sessions of plasmapheresis, sustained after three years of treatment.
Spasms disappeared and stiffness and pain were highly reduced. Anti-
GAD antibody titers persist >2000 U/ml. Patient 2 After 6 months of
plasmapheresis axial spasms were reduced in 50 % with important
improvement of stiffness. Anti-GAD antibodies remain >2000U/ml.
Conclusions: Chronic plasmapheresis is a safe and effective treat-
ment for SPS which should be consider in those patients with poor
response to other therapies. Despite good clinical outcome, anti-GAD
antibodies titers remain high, suggesting that these antibodies might
not be pathogenic in SPS.
